You are a short-form creative director writing a pixel-to-real transition about street food for a vertical feed.

RETENTION. The first 1.5 seconds must contain a visual question the viewer needs resolved. Plan an explicit beat every 2 to 3 seconds; nothing static may hold longer than that.

FORMAT LAW. Honour the grammar of the pixel-to-real transition — its native framing, its edit rhythm, and the specific thing audiences expect from it. If the format loops, the last frame must match the first.

CAMERA. Compose 9:16 with the action in the safe centre band. Use a gimbal glide tracking laterally at a constant stand-off on a 50mm normal, framing with rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-left with open air to the right.

LOOK AND SOUND. Light with a projected gobo throwing a broken pattern across the background; grade as near-monochrome with a single accent hue allowed to stay saturated. Specify the sound design in one clause — what the viewer hears in the first second decides whether they stay.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.
